questions.question: Why would a server reach for an interactive interface instead of returning ordinary tool content?
options: To let a user explore or configure something a paragraph of text cannot
To require a login step that completes before any tool call can run
To let the model silently rewrite the tool's own arguments before each call
To replace every text response in the conversation with one binary block
questions.explanation: MCP Apps exists for results a user wants to explore or configure directly, such as drilling into a chart or filling out a form, not for content a plain text answer already serves well.

questions.question: Where does a client declare that it supports interactive interfaces before any resource is fetched?
options: In a dedicated `ui/register` call the client sends before any tool list
In `io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities.extensions` on the request
In the HTTP `Accept` header, listed alongside `text/event-stream` always
In a one-time `initialize` handshake both sides complete before any request
questions.explanation: Extension support is declared per request in clientCapabilities.extensions, the same stateless pattern every capability in the 2026-07-28 protocol follows; there is no handshake or one-time registration call.

questions.question: A tool definition carries `_meta.ui.resourceUri`. What does a host do with that field?
options: Treat it as a local template path bundled with the host application
Store it as the cache key for the tool's next `structuredContent` result
Fetch the `ui://` resource it names through an ordinary `resources/read`
Open the address in a new browser tab outside the conversation entirely
questions.explanation: The field points at a ui:// resource, and a host resolves it the same way it resolves any other MCP resource, through resources/read, not through a special fetch method.

questions.question: A host fetches a `ui://` resource and its `mimeType` comes back as plain `text/html`. What should the host conclude?
options: The resource is a valid app already, since its scheme is `ui://` at all
The resource is valid as long as its `_meta.ui.csp` domains are all trusted
The resource is valid because plain `text/html` is a safe default type
The resource is not a valid app; the required profile parameter is missing
questions.explanation: Only text/html;profile=mcp-app marks a fetched resource as a renderable app; plain text/html is an ordinary HTML document the host should not treat as one, whatever the scheme says.

questions.question: A host that never declared the interactive-interface extension calls a UI-capable tool anyway. What happens?
options: The tool still returns a normal result whose text content stays useful
The server silently upgrades the request as though the extension were declared
The call fails immediately with the unknown-method error `-32601`
The host receives an `input_required` result asking it to add the extension
questions.explanation: A UI-capable tool keeps a meaningful text result for hosts that never declare the extension, and the side without support simply falls back to core behavior instead of the request failing.

questions.question: Why does an interactive interface render inside a sandboxed iframe instead of a directly embedded page?
options: So the app can freely reach the host page's cookies and local storage
So the app stays isolated from the host while privileged actions need consent
So the model can execute the app's own JavaScript in the host's context
So the server is allowed to skip returning any text content at all
questions.explanation: The sandbox keeps the app from reaching the host page's cookies, storage, or DOM directly, so a host can render a server's app without auditing it line by line, while any privileged action still crosses a consent-gated bridge.
